messages.author: d44307ab10d419d1
messages.subject: positive_infinity()
parts:
Hello.
The manual speaks about positive_infinity() but no example is provided.
Could anybody explain how to use it properly.

Thanks.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] positive_infinity()
parts:
positive_infinity() is a function. It returns the value of \infty.

It really doesn't have much purpose. One place you can use it is in a variable declaration. Suppose you have scale variable, sigma, that's lower bounded by 0. This is how I'd write it:
parameters {
  real<lower = 0> sigma;
}

You could write this, which isn't recommended, but you could still do this:
parameters {
  real<lower = 0, upper = positive_infinity()> sigma;
}

Since Stan is a language, I'm sure there are many other use cases that I haven't thought about.



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] positive_infinity()
parts:
Because users like to declare variables named
pi and e and they'd otherwise be illegal or
they'd mask the built-in values.

The generated C++ will be compiled so as
not to involve a function call at run time. It's
a wonderful language that way (but it's part of
why the compile times are so long with optimization).

- Bob
